A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PALU and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original TOFU and MUSE experiments, ablations, convergence analyses, dataset statistics, and generation examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds prefix-selection controls, Llama-2-13B experiments, and annotation-verification results.

M1.justification: Equation 4 and Algorithm 1 replace separate token sums with expectations, revising the stated loss normalization and potentially the relative weighting of its components. Sensitive-prefix selection, frozen-reference top-K selection, logit flattening, and KL preservation remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use TOFU, including its retained evaluation domains, and MUSE News and Books. The added prefix controls and larger model operate within existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The named benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. New Tables 3 and 6 introduce proportional-prefix alternatives and random-three-token suppression as comparison strategies. Full-token suppression was already examined in v1.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce 25%/50%/100% prefix budgets, random-token selection, and Llama-2-13B top-K and initial-N sweeps on TOFU forget 5%. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, ten-epoch training budget, batch size, and stated training grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends tests of the locality hypothesis through proportional-prefix sensitivity analysis (Table 3), random versus initial-token controls (Table 6), and vocabulary/prefix sensitivity on a 13B model (Tables 7–8). Earlier ablations, convergence plots, dataset analyses, and generation cases are retained.

E5.justification: Forget Quality remains based on the same KS-test p-value. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or empirical confidence intervals. Appendix A's new confidence statement is a theoretical assertion, not an empirical uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New results cover prefix ratios, token positions, 13B sensitivity, and annotation accuracy exceeding 98%. Table 6 reports FQ 0.1123 for random-three-token suppression versus 0.7126 for PALU. Existing benchmark tables and plots retain their values. The MinK++ comparison is corrected from 46.2% over DPO to 38.3% over the actual runner-up TPO.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces approximate absolute probabilities of 1/K with an epsilon-closeness statement for probabilities normalized within the top-K set, asserted with probability at least 1−delta. It also changes approximate ratio-preservation expressions into equalities. These substantively revise the formal claims, although the new probabilistic guarantee lacks a derivation or specified source of randomness.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: prefix-localized and vocabulary-localized unlearning, reduced intervention, and a superior forgetting–utility trade-off. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about dynamic prefix budgets needing better selection rules and interprets the new positional and scale controls. The MUSE discussion changes from Books to News but incorrectly claims better forgetting than Retain: 0.6443 belongs to Original, while Retain scores 0.3279 versus PALU's 0.4442. Existing principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract newly provides a code-repository link. Appendix E newly documents manual verification of TPO-style span annotations and correction of identified failures. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that earlier preprocessing differed. Hardware, optimizer, and training-budget disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including unlearning auditing, BALDRO, and additional application, safety, and reinforcement-learning work, while removing the Wuerkaixi and Zhou 2024 references. Its positioning against token-aware and entropy-based unlearning remains stable. TPO and several other publication updates refer to existing cited works.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section hierarchy are retained. Changes include local paragraph rewrites, shorter baseline descriptions, reordered metric explanations, standardized terminology, corrected cross-references, contact details, acknowledgments, and additional experimental subsections.

P2.justification: v3 adds four compact result tables, exchanges the order of existing Figures 3 and 4, relocates appendix tables, and reformats Algorithm 1. Existing figure graphics and generation-example displays are retained, with limited caption and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added positional controls, prefix-budget tests, 13B experiments, and reproducibility disclosures strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, Appendix A introduces an unsupported high-confidence guarantee, and Appendix F.3 replaces an accurate Books comparison with an incorrect News-versus-Retain claim. These gains and losses affect scientific support and reliability, leaving the net overall quality direction uncertain.
